# Linux Network Bandwidth and Connection Testing

Network issues should be categorized into three types of checks: process occupancy, end-to-end throughput, and external network connectivity. This page uses `nethogs`, `iperf3`, and `curl` to identify problems respectively.

## View process bandwidth

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nethogs
sudo nethogs
```

The interface will display the real-time upload and download speeds by process. Exit by `q`.

![nethogs Process Bandwidth Interface ](../../11-其他辅助工具/assets/image-20251026115247175.png)

## Test the throughput between two machines

Install `iperf3` on both machines first:

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y iperf3
```

Server execution:

```bash
iperf3 -s
```

Client execution:

```bash
iperf3 -c <SERVER_IP> -P 4
```

## Verification and Debugging

If the system has not installed `curl`, execute first:

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y curl
```

```bash
curl -I --connect-timeout 10 https://github.com
ip route
```

`iperf3` indicates the local network transmission capacity between two machines. `curl` checks the connection and response of a specified website. `nethogs` shows the bandwidth used by various processes on the local machine. These three types of results cannot be replaced by each other.

If the domain access fails but the IP works, check the DNS configuration. If `iperf3` cannot connect, verify the server port and firewall rules. If only a single process uses all the bandwidth, go back to `nethogs` to identify the process and then adjust the concurrency level.
